Banking Platform — Core Documentation vs Implementation

Traceability backlog mapping blueprint set v3.1 (Docs 00–29, feature specs, design companions, ADRs) to the banking-platform monorepo as of 17 August 2026. Analysis only — application source was not modified. Intended for product owners, BAs, PMs, developers, QA, and technical leads.

1. Executive summary

This analysis reviewed all 57 Word documents in documentation/Banking_Takaful_Platform_Documentation (29 blueprints, 24 feature specs, 3 plans, 1 presenter script), all 30 design.md companions, ADR-0002 in the documentation set, repo ADRs 0003–0006, and the current source tree (services, JVM, packages, apps, infra). Presentations (.pptx) were inventoried as non-requirements. Takaful content is recorded as out of scope for this repository (ADR-0003).

The repo is past Sprint 0: it is a login-to-money-movement pilot on a local stack — Control Plane, Identity (retail + mock eKYC), Wallets, Ledger L1–L5 (TigerBeetle), Pricing quotes, Payments saga (PK-PK simulated rail + on-us), Screening (transaction + HIGH maker-checker), BFF, customer web app, and staff console. That is substantially more than a scaffold, and substantially less than the documented PK go-live bar.

Major gaps vs documentation: no real NADRA/Raast/OIDC/tax/notification/reporting/reconciliation; persistence isolation router and KSA residency not enforced; no CI; most SPI adapters are mocks or absent; Cards/CBS deferred by the programme plan; customer UI covers a narrow on-us demo, not remittance corridors or statements; Pricing emits silent zero tax (conflicts with fail-closed).

Counts: 31 Done, 63 Partially Done, 214 Not Started, 1 Unclear, 2 Out of Scope. Priority mix: Critical 58, High 122, Low 42, Medium 89.

2. Repository analysis summary

  • Runtime: Nx monorepo (ADR-0003). NestJS/TS services + Java 21 Ledger/Pricing/FX. Node 22, PostgreSQL 16, TigerBeetle, Redpanda, Redis.
  • Present services: services/control-plane, identity, wallets, payments, screening, bff; jvm/ledger, jvm/pricing, jvm/libs/{fx,money,persistence}.
  • Absent services: notification, compliance-reporting, reconciliation, cards — plus standalone adapters/ provider apps (folder has AGENTS.md only).
  • Apps: apps/web (customer: auth, dashboard, send, top-up, profile, help) and apps/console (staff: tenants, branding).
  • Packages: money, http-kit, auth-kit, persistence (ports + TODO router), tsconfig, design-tokens. Missing: telemetry, oidc, pact-fixtures.
  • Auth: HS256 JWT stand-in, one shared secret (ADR-0006). Not Design 22 Keycloak/JWKS.
  • Contracts: three Pact files verified live; no OpenAPI tree; no CI.
  • Local infra: compose + start-dev.sh + per-tenant provisioner (silo-like DBs). Known gap: Payments/Screening still target the shared Ledger for newly provisioned tenants.

3. Documentation summary

Authoritative specs are the .docx blueprints + .design.md companions (v3.1). Feature specs add MoSCoW catalogues used as the primary task grain in this backlog (one task per catalogue row, plus extras for UI/CI/events not given their own row).

  • 00–01: architecture invariants, stack (NestJS default, JVM islands 04/10/17).
  • 02–13: twelve services (04 & 10 Java).
  • 14–22, 24–26: persistence + SPI adapters (17 is a Java library; 18/20 deferred until a tenant needs them).
  • 23, 27–29: index, git/CI, repo catalog (superseded by ADR-0003 monorepo), programme plan M0–M8.
  • Ledger plans: L0–L5 — L1 through L5 are implemented in jvm/ledger.
  • ADR-0002: FX provenance; D7 PKR-only pilot (FX conversion built, not activated).
  • Launch markets: PK → AE → SA. Critical path: Control Plane → Ledger → Pricing+FX → Payments+Rail → PK go-live.

Documents inventoried but not turned into product tasks: 06_Presentations/* (review decks + Roman Urdu script). Takaful-only requirements are Out of Scope here.

4. Complete requirements & task matrix

Working order (last column, 1 = first) is the recommended build sequence: specific catalogue dependencies (e.g. CR2 after CR1, 04 HD1) are done first, then the Doc 23/29 critical path (Control Plane → Ledger → Pricing → Payments). Already-done tickets get earlier numbers so remaining work follows completed dependencies. Choose Sort by working order to walk the table top-to-bottom in that sequence. Ticket ID stays the stable BANK-xxx number.

Dependencies column. Comma-separated things this ticket needs before it can be finished. A two-digit number is a document / capability (02 Identity, 03 Screening, 04 Ledger, 05 Payments, 06 Wallets, 10 Pricing, 11 BFF, 12 Control Plane, 14 Persistence, 16 eKYC, 19 Payout rail, … — same numbers as in the Module column). A code like VF4 or AC4 is a feature-catalogue id from that spec (shown in the Task column, e.g. “AC4 — Close account”). Combined forms: 16 VF4 = eKYC adapter’s VF4 (business-registry lookup); 06 AC4 = Wallets close-account; CR2 alone = another feature in the same module. Words like packs mean Control Plane compliance/config packs, not a ticket id. Empty = no documented predecessor.

BANK-001 Work #163

CR1 — Retail customer registration

Partially Done Critical Must Ready

Identity, KYC/KYB & Onboarding (02) · services/identity

Requirement / business context
Create a customer with minimal PII, generate a canonical CustomerId, emit registered event
Detailed description

This service is the system of record for customers (retail) and businesses (corporate/KYB), and for the verification cases that prove their identity. It computes and maintains a risk tier per customer from verification outcomes, screening signals, geography and product, and it drives the onboarding workflow from first application to activated relationship. Everything it does is scoped by the tenant's assigned.

This ticket is CR1 — Retail customer registration (Must). The feature specification requires: Create a customer with minimal PII, generate a canonical CustomerId, emit registered event.

Specified rules: Every customer and business is uniquely and immutably identified; identity keys are the national IDs per market, never free-text names. A verification-case timeout or provider error moves the case to MANUAL_REVIEW; the service never auto-approves on failure (fail-safe). Verification evidence (images, biometrics) is stored only as an object-storage reference; PII blobs never sit inline in the service database. Risk tier is recomputed deterministically whenever an input changes; the same inputs always yield the same tier. Contract surface: - POST /v1/customers · POST /v1/customers/{id}/verifications · POST /v1/verifications/{caseId}/evidence. - GET /v1/customers/{id}/risk-tier · POST /v1/businesses/{id}/ubos. - GET /v1/customers/{id}/onboarding (status + SLA). Events: identity.customer.registered.v1, identity.verification.completed.v1, identity.risk_tier.changed.v1, screening.case.resolved.v1. Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Customers (retail) — identity, status, current risk tier. - Businesses + UBOs — entity, registration, beneficial owners and their. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Customer (or Business) profile, with an attached VerificationCase representing one identity-verification journey. Design companion: Fail-safe: provider timeout ⇒ case → `MANUAL_REVIEW`, never auto-approve.

What exists today: POST /v1/customers and POST /v1/auth/register in services/identity (RegisterCustomerService, AuthRegisterService). Customer aggregate persists to Postgres. BFF auto-registers customers. Remaining work to match the documentation: Does not emit identity.customer.registered.v1 (no outbox). Screening is not called at register time (Design 02 sequence). Kind is retail-only in practice. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes. Retail path exists; events and onboarding screen are the remaining Musts.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What was found in the repository: `services/identity/src/application/register-customer.service.ts`, `src/adapters/rest/identity.controller.ts` (`POST v1/customers` → 201 + customerId), `src/domain/customer.ts` (`Customer.register` → UNRATED/PENDING_VERIFICATION), branded `CustomerId` in `src/domain/ids.ts`. Verified live per README. This was verified live against the local stack, not only by reading source.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Create a customer with minimal PII, generate a canonical CustomerId, set tier UNRATED, emit `identity.customer.registered.v1`.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: No `identity.customer.registered.v1` event (no outbox/Kafka wired). No PII captured at registration beyond `kind` (name/email live on the separate `credentials` table); no national-ID identity key (FS 02 §4: "identity keys are the national IDs per market"). No Idempotency-Key. Registration path is real (NestJS + Postgres) and consumed by Wallets' `IdentityBackedRulesAdapter`, but it registers an anonymous shell, not a KYC-grade identity record.

Source of this assessment: documentation-vs-code gap analysis for «Retail customer registration (CR1)».

Gap / missing work
Does not emit identity.customer.registered.v1 (no outbox). Screening is not called at register time (Design 02 sequence). Kind is retail-only in practice.
Acceptance criteria
  • POST /v1/customers creates a tenant-scoped customer with a canonical id and UNRATED tier
  • identity.customer.registered.v1 is published via transactional outbox
  • Onboarding-time entity screening is invoked; failure holds, never auto-clears
Dependencies
16, 03, 14
Working order
163 of 311 — work in this sequence so listed dependencies and the critical path are already in place.
Technical notes
Retail path exists; events and onboarding screen are the remaining Musts.

Requirement / business context
Screen a customer/counterparty synchronously; return hits + score + list version
Detailed description

This service screens customers and counterparties against sanctions, PEP and adverse-media lists, runs transaction-monitoring scenarios, and manages the resulting investigation cases to disposition. It is the single compliance gate for both applications: onboarding calls it, every transfer calls it, and every takaful participant, beneficiary and claim payee passes through it. Its behaviour is defined entirely by the.

This ticket is SC1 — Real-time entity screening (Must). The feature specification requires: Screen a customer/counterparty synchronously; return hits + score + list version.

Specified rules: Every screening result stores the exact list version used, enabling audit replay. A screening timeout, circuit-open or provider error returns HOLD and queues for review — never CLEAR (fail-safe closed). List scope per market comes from the pack (minimum: UN Consolidated, OFAC SDN, plus NACTA / UAE local list / KSA designated persons). Case data is DB-/schema-isolated per tenant regardless of general tier. Contract surface: - POST /v1/screening/entities · POST /v1/screening/transactions. - GET /v1/cases/{id} · POST /v1/cases/{id}/disposition (maker-checker on high). Events: screening.case.opened.v1, screening.case.resolved.v1, screening.transaction.flagged.v1, identity.customer.registered.v1, payments.transfer.initiated.v1. Domain invariant: The core aggregates are the ScreeningRequest (a single check) and the Case (an investigation opened from one or more hits). Design companion: **Runtime:** NestJS 10 / TS strict · **Squad:** Compliance & AML · **DB:** PostgreSQL 16 + OpenSearch · **Docx:** `03_Service_Screening_AML_Service.docx` Compliance gate for onboarding and every money movement. List scope per pack — launch minimum: UN Consolidated, OFAC SDN, plus domestic lists (PK NACTA proscribed persons, UAE Local Terrorist List, KSA designated persons). **Fail-safe closed:** a screening failure is a HOLD.

JP1 — Balanced journal post

Done Critical Must Ready

Ledger (04) · jvm/ledger

Requirement / business context
Accept a set of debits/credits that sum to zero per currency; reject if unbalanced
Detailed description

This service is the system of record for value across the whole platform. It records money as balanced, double-entry, append-only journals; balances are projections derived from postings, never stored-and-mutated. It deliberately runs on the JVM for BigDecimal/integer-minor-unit exactness and throughput on the posting hot path. Both applications post to it: banking transactions and card holds, and takaful.

This ticket is JP1 — Balanced journal post (Must). The feature specification requires: Accept a set of debits/credits that sum to zero per currency; reject if unbalanced.

Specified rules: A journal that does not balance to zero per currency is rejected in the domain and never persisted. A cross-currency conversion is one journal whose currency groups each sum to zero, bridged by FX position accounts, with the spread recognised in the customer's funding currency. Posting is idempotent: the same idempotency key yields the identical journal and never double-posts. Every post emits an event via the transactional outbox in the same transaction as the write. Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Journals — balanced, append-only, idempotency-keyed; carrying quote_id and display_meta (ADR-0002). - Postings — the immutable. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Journal (a balanced set of postings). Account is a projection, not a source of truth. Design companion: - **Provenance (D1):** `rate_mid` / margin / customer rate stay authoritative in `quotes.fx_snapshot` (Design 10). `journals.quote_id` is the audit link. The Ledger is never a second source of truth for rates. - **Statement fields (D2):** `journals.display_meta` snapshots. - **Pilot scope (D7):** PK inbound remittance books PKR only (conversion happens at the corridor boundary). `FX_CONVERSION` and the position accounts are built behind a capability flag, activated when multi-currency wallets ship.

What is already in the repository: Journal.balanced(...) rejects unbalanced sets per currency. POST /v1/journals. jqwik properties. Verified live. The documented Must for this ticket is implemented. Keep regression coverage against the acceptance criteria; do not re-implement it. L1–L2 complete.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: correctly implemented against the documented Must. The code path was inspected and matches the specification for this ticket. Keep regression coverage; do not rebuild it.

What was found in the repository: `jvm/ledger/src/main/java/com/platform/ledger/domain/Journal.java` (`Journal.balanced()`/`construct()` — per-currency `Math.addExact` sums, `UnbalancedJournalException(offending)`); `JournalTest`, `JournalProperties` (jqwik fuzzing: any unbalanced line set throws); rejected as 422 via `adapters/rest/ApiExceptionHandler`.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: A journal is a balanced set of postings; debits = credits **per currency independently**; an unbalanced journal is rejected in the domain and never persisted.

Analyst notes: TigerBeetle's own debits=credits enforcement is defence-in-depth (ADR-0004), not a substitute — domain validation runs first, as ADR-0004 requires.

Source of this assessment: documentation-vs-code gap analysis for «Balanced double-entry journal post (sum-to-zero per currency)».

JP2 — Idempotent posting

Ledger (04) · jvm/ledger

Requirement / business context
Same idempotency key returns the same journal; one row only
Detailed description

This service is the system of record for value across the whole platform. It records money as balanced, double-entry, append-only journals; balances are projections derived from postings, never stored-and-mutated. It deliberately runs on the JVM for BigDecimal/integer-minor-unit exactness and throughput on the posting hot path. Both applications post to it: banking transactions and card holds, and takaful.

This ticket is JP2 — Idempotent posting (Must). The feature specification requires: Same idempotency key returns the same journal; one row only.

Specified rules: Posting is idempotent: the same idempotency key yields the identical journal and never double-posts. A journal that does not balance to zero per currency is rejected in the domain and never persisted. Every post emits an event via the transactional outbox in the same transaction as the write. Rates are never managed here: Pricing (10) locks the rate and it arrives as an input to the posting. The posting path must never call FxRatePort (ADR-0002 D6, ArchUnit-enforced). Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Journals — balanced, append-only, idempotency-keyed; carrying quote_id and display_meta (ADR-0002). - Postings — the immutable. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Journal (a balanced set of postings). Account is a projection, not a source of truth. Design companion: System of record for value. Double-entry, append-only; balances are projections. Nothing else on the platform may hold a balance. Stays on the JVM for BigDecimal/long-minor-unit exactness, ArchUnit, and throughput on the posting hot path. Rounding: `HALF_EVEN` for balance-affecting derivations; contract-specified mode at explicit fee/FX posting points only — `Money.applyRate(BigDecimal, RoundingMode)` is the sole decimal gateway.

What is already in the repository: UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key). Retry completes PENDING journals. TigerBeetle Exists dedup. Verified live. The documented Must for this ticket is implemented. Keep regression coverage against the acceptance criteria; do not re-implement it.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: correctly implemented against the documented Must. The code path was inspected and matches the specification for this ticket. Keep regression coverage; do not rebuild it.

What was found in the repository: `V1__baseline.sql` `UNIQUE (tenant_id, idempotency_key)` on `journals` and `holds`; `JournalCommandService.post()` replays via `byIdempotencyKey` and `ensurePosted()` (completes an interrupted write on retry, not just returns it); TB transfer ids deterministic from journal id (`TigerBeetleGateway.deterministicTransferId`, `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(journalId:index)`) so replay is a TB `Exists` no-op; `JournalCommandServiceTest`; README live verification (retry converged, no duplicate transfer).

What 'correct' means per the documentation: The same idempotency key returns the identical journal and never double-posts; one row only, on any retry.

Analyst notes: Idempotency at *both* layers (PG unique constraint + TB deterministic ids) exactly as ADR-0004 specifies.

Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Journals — balanced, append-only, idempotency-keyed; carrying quote_id and display_meta (ADR-0002). - Postings — the immutable. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Journal (a balanced set of postings). Account is a projection, not a source of truth. Design companion: - **Provenance (D1):** `rate_mid` / margin / customer rate stay authoritative in `quotes.fx_snapshot` (Design 10). `journals.quote_id` is the audit link. The Ledger is never a second source of truth for rates. - **Statement fields (D2):** `journals.display_meta` snapshots. - **Pilot scope (D7):** PK inbound remittance books PKR only (conversion happens at the corridor boundary). `FX_CONVERSION` and the position accounts are built behind a capability flag, activated when multi-currency wallets ship.

What exists today: FX_CONVERSION type and position accounts exist. JournalCommandService rejects multi-currency unless ledger.multi-currency-enabled (default false, ADR-0002 D7). Remaining work to match the documentation: Capability flag is deployment-wide, not per-tenant from Control Plane. PK pilot is PKR-only. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes. Built, not activated matches D7.

All amounts are integer minor units; no floating-point arithmetic exists anywhere in the service. Posting is idempotent: the same idempotency key yields the identical journal and never double-posts. Rates are never managed here: Pricing (10) locks the rate and it arrives as an input to the posting. The posting path must never call FxRatePort (ADR-0002 D6, ArchUnit-enforced). Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Journals — balanced, append-only, idempotency-keyed; carrying quote_id and display_meta (ADR-0002). - Postings — the immutable. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Journal (a balanced set of postings). Account is a projection, not a source of truth. Design companion: System of record for value. Double-entry, append-only; balances are projections. Nothing else on the platform may hold a balance. Stays on the JVM for BigDecimal/long-minor-unit exactness, ArchUnit, and throughput on the posting hot path.

What is already in the repository: POST /v1/holds, TigerBeetle PENDING transfer, holds.suspense self-provision. PLACE-phase recovery sweeper chaos-tested. The documented Must for this ticket is implemented. Keep regression coverage against the acceptance criteria; do not re-implement it.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: correctly implemented against the documented Must. The code path was inspected and matches the specification for this ticket. Keep regression coverage; do not rebuild it.

What was found in the repository: `domain/Hold.java` state machine (PLACED → CAPTURED | RELEASED, `IllegalHoldTransitionException` → 409); `application/HoldCommandService.java` (idempotency convergence on placement key / `hasEvent`); `TigerBeetleGateway.placePendingTransfer/postPendingTransfer/voidPendingTransfer` (TB two-phase transfers, `AMOUNT_MAX` sentinel on post, deterministic per-(holdId, phase) ids); `PostgresHoldRepository` (append-only `hold_status_events`); `HoldController` → `POST /v1/holds`, `/v1/holds/{id}/capture`, `/v1/holds/{id}/release`; `HoldCommandServiceTest`, `HoldTest`; README live verification incl. suspense-account balance math.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Place a hold reserving available balance; capture converts it into a posting; release frees it without posting. All idempotent; exactly one terminal state.

Residual notes (not a Must-gap for this ticket): capture/release have no *automatic* recovery backstop (only PLACE has a sweeper — `HoldRecoveryService` javadoc explains why); a client retry with the same key still converges correctly. Blueprint modeled holds as rows + scheduled job; ADR-0004 remapped to TB pending transfers — implementation follows the ADR.

Ledger (04) · jvm/ledger

Requirement / business context
One journal, per-currency groups each summing to zero, bridged by FX-Position-<ccy>
Detailed description

This service is the system of record for value across the whole platform. It records money as balanced, double-entry, append-only journals; balances are projections derived from postings, never stored-and-mutated. It deliberately runs on the JVM for BigDecimal/integer-minor-unit exactness and throughput on the posting hot path. Both applications post to it: banking transactions and card holds, and takaful.

This ticket is FX4 — FX_CONVERSION journal type (Should). The feature specification requires: One journal, per-currency groups each summing to zero, bridged by FX-Position-<ccy>.

Specified rules: A cross-currency conversion is one journal whose currency groups each sum to zero, bridged by FX position accounts, with the spread recognised in the customer's funding currency. A journal that does not balance to zero per currency is rejected in the domain and never persisted. Posting is idempotent: the same idempotency key yields the identical journal and never double-posts. A journal from a priced operation carries quote_id (audit link) and display_meta (reproducible statement fields); the quote remains authoritative for the rate. Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Journal (a balanced set of postings). Account is a projection, not a source of truth. Design companion: - **Provenance (D1):** `rate_mid` / margin / customer rate stay authoritative in `quotes.fx_snapshot` (Design 10). `journals.quote_id` is the audit link. The Ledger is never a second source of truth for rates. - **Statement fields (D2):** `journals.display_meta` snapshots. - **Pilot scope (D7):** PK inbound remittance books PKR only (conversion happens at the corridor boundary). `FX_CONVERSION` and the position accounts are built behind a capability flag, activated when multi-currency wallets ship.

What exists today: JournalType.FX_CONVERSION and FX-Position CoA entries exist; rejected unless flag on. Remaining work to match the documentation: Activate per tenant when multi-currency wallets ship. Wire quote_id on the conversion journal. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: `FX-Position-<ccy>` accounts cannot actually be materialized yet — `GetSystemAccountService` refuses `perCurrency=true` refs (404) because per-currency materialization is deferred; so activating the flag today would fail at the first conversion. "Built, not activated" is honest, but "activatable" needs the perCurrency materialization work first.

Specified rules: A journal that does not balance to zero per currency is rejected in the domain and never persisted. All amounts are integer minor units; no floating-point arithmetic exists anywhere in the service. Posting is idempotent: the same idempotency key yields the identical journal and never double-posts. Rates are never managed here: Pricing (10) locks the rate and it arrives as an input to the posting. The posting path must never call FxRatePort (ADR-0002 D6, ArchUnit-enforced). Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Journals — balanced, append-only, idempotency-keyed; carrying quote_id and display_meta (ADR-0002). - Postings — the immutable. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Journal (a balanced set of postings). Account is a projection, not a source of truth. Design companion: System of record for value. Double-entry, append-only; balances are projections. Nothing else on the platform may hold a balance. Stays on the JVM for BigDecimal/long-minor-unit exactness, ArchUnit, and throughput on the posting hot path. Rounding: `HALF_EVEN` for balance-affecting derivations; contract-specified mode at explicit fee/FX posting points only — `Money.applyRate(BigDecimal, RoundingMode)` is the sole decimal gateway.

What is already in the repository: GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance?asOf= ISO-8601. TigerBeetle HISTORY flag. Verified live. The documented Must for this ticket is implemented. Keep regression coverage against the acceptance criteria; do not re-implement it. Should in spec; implemented.

Release the Ledger hold; transfer → failed
Detailed description

This service coordinates a domestic or cross-border money transfer as a persisted, idempotent saga. It gets a quote, screens the transaction, places a hold on funds, executes the payout via the bound rail, and settles — with an explicit compensation path for every failure mode. Launch corridors are UAE→Pakistan and KSA→Pakistan (the primary remittance use case) plus domestic transfers via Raast, Aani and sarie.

This ticket is CP2 — Compensation on rail-reject (Must). The feature specification requires: Release the Ledger hold; transfer → failed.

Specified rules: All amounts use integer minor units end-to-end; the only synchronous money write is the Ledger hold. Each failure mode triggers a specific, idempotent compensation step; funds are never left stranded. IN_FLIGHT is a first-class state — a rail timeout is resolved by a status-inquiry job, never guessed. Every saga step is a persisted, idempotent state transition; out-of-order retries cannot corrupt state. Contract surface: - POST /v1/transfers (202) · GET /v1/transfers/{id} · POST /v1/transfers/{id}/cancel. - POST /v1/beneficiaries (corridor-validated). Events: screening.case.resolved.v1. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Transfer, which owns a saga state machine spanning quote through settlement. Design companion: Orchestrates the send-money saga: quote → screen → hold → payout → confirm, with explicit compensation. Launch corridors: **UAE→PK, KSA→PK** (primary), reverse, and domestic via Raast (PK) / Aani (AE) / sarie (SA). Saga = persisted state machine + choreography — no heavyweight. Compensations: screen-fail⇒cancel quote (C1) · rail-reject⇒release hold (C2) · settlement-fail⇒reverse journal + rail refund path (C3). Each is an idempotent saga step in `saga_steps`.

What is already in the repository: Rail REJECT → releaseHold, FAILED, balance untouched. Verified live. The documented Must for this ticket is implemented. Keep regression coverage against the acceptance criteria; do not re-implement it.

Data owned by this service: This component is the system of record for the following (all rows tenant-scoped; app_id present where the component is a shared adapter): - Products — versioned account product templates. - Accounts — customer accounts and their ledger-account mapping. - Statements — immutable. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Account, an instance of a configured Product template, linked 1:1 with one or more Ledger accounts (one per currency held). Design companion: Customer-facing account layer: product instances, statements, balance views. **Never holds value** — every balance is composed from Ledger (04). Balance view: Redis cache keyed `tenant:account:ccy`, invalidated by consuming `ledger.journal.posted.v1` (target: within the 2 s outbox-lag budget).

Detailed description

This optional-capability service issues virtual and physical cards, manages spend controls, and answers real-time authorization requests within the processor's time window. It never stores raw PANs — only tokenised references — so PCI scope stays at the processor. On any doubt or timeout it declines (fail-safe closed).

This ticket is AU2 — Real-time authorization (Must). The feature specification requires: Decide approve/decline within the processor window on the Fastify path.

Specified rules: Any timeout or error on the authorization path results in DECLINE. The authorization path performs one synchronous call (the Ledger hold); everything else is pre-computed/cached. Authorization handling is idempotent across duplicate processor callbacks. Raw PANs never touch platform storage or logs; only tokenised references are stored. Contract surface: - POST /v1/cards · POST /v1/cards/{id}/freeze · PUT /v1/cards/{id}/controls. Events: cards.card.issued.v1, cards.authorization.declined.v1, wallets.account.closed.v1. Domain invariant: The core aggregate is the Card, linked to exactly one Account and governed by a set of SpendControls. Design companion: **Runtime:** NestJS 10 / TS strict — **authorization webhook on FastifyAdapter** · **Squad:** Accounts & Cards · **Docx:** `07_Service_Card_Issuing_Service_Optional_Capability.docx` Virtual/physical issuance + real-time authorization via processor adapter (20). Tokenised refs only — raw PAN never touches platform storage (PCI scope reduction). **Timeout ⇒ DECLINE** (fail-safe closed).

No meaningful implementation was found (No services/cards directory. Doc 29 defers Cards (07)+processor (20) until a tenant licenses them). Implement this feature as specified. Concretely: Implement Real-time authorization per Design 07. Timeout ⇒ DECLINE. Tokenised refs only; no PAN in storage or logs. Sequenced after PK money path. Not out of product scope.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: not implemented. No meaningful implementation of this requirement was found in the repository.

What was found in the repository: none found — no webhook, no Fastify adapter, no `AuthorizationDecision`. The Ledger-side `placeHold` prerequisite exists (jvm/ledger holds, L3).

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Authorization webhook decides approve/decline within the processor window (p99 < 400 ms platform-side); any timeout or error ⇒ DECLINE, never approve; the only synchronous dependency is the Ledger hold; approved-then-declined holds are released asynchronously.

Nothing to assess as 'correct' until the feature is built. Specified remaining work: The entire hot path, its caches (card status, controls), the compensating hold-release, and the fault-injection tests. This is one of the root AGENTS.md §1.8 named fail-closed invariants — it must be treated as release-blocking for any future cards build, and the timeout-⇒-DECLINE test should exist before the happy path.

Source of this assessment: documentation-vs-code gap analysis for «Real-time authorization — fail-safe DECLINE on timeout/error».

Requirement / business context
Return base/fee/commission/FX-margin/tax/promo lines + total
Detailed description

This service produces deterministic, explainable quotes — base amount, fees, commission, FX margin, tax and promotions — and meters usage for invoicing. It runs on the JVM for exact BigDecimal arithmetic and consumes the FX rate library (17) in-process, so there is no network hop on the quote path. Both apps use it: banking fees/commission and takaful contribution/wakala-fee pricing.

This ticket is QT1 — Itemised quote (Must). The feature specification requires: Return base/fee/commission/FX-margin/tax/promo lines + total.

Specified rules: Every quote line is traceable to a rule (and version); the breakdown sums exactly to the total. Same inputs + same rule-pack/rate snapshot = byte-identical quote (determinism). The FX library is consumed in-process — no network call on the quote hot path. All arithmetic is BigDecimal / integer minor units; no floats. Contract surface: - POST /v1/quotes · POST /v1/usage (idempotent) · GET /v1/invoices/{tenant}/{period}. Events: pricing.quote.issued.v1, billing.invoice.generated.v1, payments.transfer.completed.v1, screening.case.opened.v1. Domain invariant: The core aggregates are the Quote (a point-in-time computed price) and the UsageRecord (a metered billable event). Design companion: Deterministic, explainable quotes (fees, commission, FX margin, tax, promotions) + usage metering → invoicing. Stays on the JVM: BigDecimal quote math, ArchUnit, and it consumes the FX adapter (17) **in-process** — no network hop on the quote path.

What exists today: Quote/QuoteLine/QuoteCalculator. Breakdown BASE/FEE/TAX/(FX_MARGIN). UnbalancedQuoteException. POST /v1/quotes. jqwik. Live REMITTANCE + FX_CONVERSION quotes. Remaining work to match the documentation: COMMISSION and PROMO line types unused. Tax is a hardcoded 0.00, not adapter 25. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Requirement / business context
Resolve tenant_id/app_id/channel from the validated token and route
Detailed description

This is the platform's public and partner surface. It resolves which tenant and channel a request belongs to, enforces OAuth2 scopes, composes backends-for-frontends (BFFs) for mobile/web/partner, manages outbound webhooks, offers a sandbox, generates SDKs, and applies localization and per-tenant theming. BFFs compose domain services; they never re-implement domain logic.

This ticket is GW1 — Tenant & channel resolution (Must). The feature specification requires: Resolve tenant_id/app_id/channel from the validated token and route.

Specified rules: Every request has its tenant/app/channel resolved before reaching any service; a missing tenant claim is rejected. Locale resolution follows the chain and applies RTL for ur-PK / ar-AE / ar-SA. The sandbox is structurally isolated (separate namespaces/data), never a flag on production rows. Contract surface: - Gateway routes all /v1/* after resolution · POST /v1/webhooks · GET /.well-known/openapi.json · sandbox reset. Events: - Publishes: platform.webhook.delivered|failed.v1. - Consumes: all domain topics (to fan out to subscribed webhooks). Domain invariant: This service is largely an orchestration/composition layer; its primary owned entities are Webhook subscriptions and SandboxTenants. Design companion: The public/partner surface: tenant/channel resolution, OAuth2 scope enforcement (via 22), webhooks, sandbox, SDK generation, localization + theming composition. **BFFs compose; they never re-implement domain logic** (review checklist rule). Locale chain (launch): request `Accept-Language` → user pref → tenant default → `en-*` fallback; RTL flag for `ur-PK` (Nastaliq), `ar-AE`, `ar-SA`. Design tokens per tenant injected into composed responses/templates.

What exists today: services/bff verifies JWT (auth-kit), extracts tenant_id/customer. apps/web bakes VITE_TENANT_ID per deploy. Caddy *.localhost routes for provisioned tenants. Remaining work to match the documentation: No Kong. No channel claim. Downstream services still trust X-Tenant-Id (ADR-0006: safe only because BFF is the trust boundary). Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Resolve tenant, app, and channel from the validated token before any service is reached; context flows to every downstream call.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: No channel or app_id concept anywhere (single web channel assumed); no AsyncLocalStorage — tenant context is passed by hand per call, workable at this size but not the design's ambient-context pattern; correlation id only forwarded on the two auth routes, not systematically. Domain invariant: Core aggregates are Tenant, ConfigurationVersion and Entitlement. Design companion: **Runtime:** NestJS 10 / TS strict · **Squad:** Platform / Enablement · **DB:** PostgreSQL 16 + Redis (+ in-process LRU) · **Docx:** `12_Service_Tenant_Registry_Control_Plane_Service.docx` The tenant-agnostic brain: registry, hierarchical config store/resolver, entitlements, onboarding orchestration. Holds **no regulated customer data**. Hot path (`resolveEffectiveConfig`) is every service's dependency — treated tier-critical; consumers fail safe on cache-stale.

What exists today: Tenant register/activate/suspend with maker-checker on suspend. POST /v1/tenants, activate, suspend. Status PROVISIONING→ACTIVE. Staff auth. GET list. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Error classification is proper RFC 7807 (`error-mapping.ts`: 404 unknown-tenant, 409 state conflicts, 400 same-actor).

For a local build this substantially *exceeds* what most pilots have — real SILO isolation per tenant, exercised from the console UI.

Requirement / business context
Call the vendor to screen an entity; return normalized hits
Detailed description

This adapter wraps a bound sanctions/PEP/adverse-media vendor and translates its match model into the platform's normalized ScreeningResult. Vendor choice is per-tenant SPI configuration. Fail-safe-closed is the consuming service's rule; this adapter's job is to return honest results and honest errors — it never turns a timeout into a CLEAR.

This ticket is SC1 — Entity screening (Must). The feature specification requires: Call the vendor to screen an entity; return normalized hits.

Specified rules: Multiple vendor mappers produce the identical normalized shape (verified by parity fixtures). A timeout, circuit-open or vendor error throws a distinct ProviderUnavailable error — never a synthetic CLEAR. Every result carries the vendor's list version for audit replay by the service. Vendor scores are mapped into the platform's 0–1 range via a per-vendor calibration table. Events: - Publishes/consumes: none (synchronous port; the service owns events). Design companion: **Impl (v3.1):** TypeScript — NestJS injectable providers · **Consumer:** Screening & AML (03) · **Docx:** `15_Adapter_Screening_AML_Provider_Adapter_Specification.docx` Translates a bound vendor's match model into the platform's `ScreeningResult`. Vendor choice is per-tenant SPI configuration. **Fail-safe closed is the consumer's rule; this adapter's job is honest errors** — it never converts a timeout into a CLEAR.

What exists today: ScreeningProviderPort + FixedWatchlistProviderAdapter (SANCTIONED substring). Fail-closed. Remaining work to match the documentation: Not a hexagonal adapter app under adapters/. No vendor. No normalized score/list version. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What was found in the repository: The only implementations are placeholders: `services/screening/src/adapters/external/fixed-watchlist-provider.adapter.ts` (substring `"SANCTIONED"` ⇒ hit, `fixed-test-list`), `services/payments/src/adapters/external/simple-screening.adapter.ts` (now replaced in Payments' wiring by `HttpScreeningClient` but still present), and `services/identity/src/adapters/external/trivial-screening.adapter.ts` (always CLEAR). Root AGENTS.md §9 admits "trivial/always-clear screening" as a known placeholder. `adapters/` directory contains only `AGENTS.md`.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Wrap a real sanctions/PEP/adverse-media vendor; normalize vendor hits to `{listName, matchedName, matchStrength 0..1, listEntryRef}` via a per-vendor calibration table; vendor shape never leaks through the port.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: No vendor integration, no mapper, no calibration, no normalized hit model. The placeholders are honestly labelled and the port boundary is respected — the swap-the-adapter path is intact.

Source of this assessment: documentation-vs-code gap analysis for «Real vendor adapter with anti-corruption normalization and score calibration».

RT1 — Current mid-rate

FX Rate Adapter (17) · jvm/libs/fx

Requirement / business context
Return the mid-market rate for a pair, or throw if stale
Detailed description

This adapter serves current (and, where needed, historical) exchange rates as raw mid-market rates. Margin/spread is applied afterwards by Pricing, never here. It is a Java library consumed in-process by Ledger and Pricing — deliberately not a network service — so the quote path has no FX network hop. It guards against stale and fat-finger rates by failing closed.

This ticket is RT1 — Current mid-rate (Must). The feature specification requires: Return the mid-market rate for a pair, or throw if stale.

Specified rules: Rates are raw mid-market only; no margin is ever applied inside this adapter. A rate older than the staleness tolerance throws rather than returning a last-good value silently. A rate outside the sanity band is rejected (fat-finger guard); quoting halts (fail closed). It returns BigDecimal rates and never rounds money. Events: - Publishes/consumes: none (in-process library). Data owned by this service: This adapter owns no persistent business data; it caches and validates rates in memory. It manages: - None persisted long-term — it caches rates in-process. Historical rates come from the feed, not a store it owns. Design companion: Serves raw **mid-market** rates; margin/spread is Pricing's job, never applied here. Launch pairs: PKR↔USD, PKR↔AED, PKR↔SAR, AED↔USD, SAR↔USD, AED↔SAR (UAE→PK and KSA→PK corridors first).

What exists today: FxRatePort.midRate + FixedTableFxRatePort (AED/PKR 76.50, USD pegs). Used by Pricing FX_CONVERSION. Remaining work to match the documentation: No commercial-primary feed. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: Rule is binary — `APPROVED+CLEAR → LOW`, else `HIGH`; MEDIUM is unreachable; geography and product are not inputs; no contributing-factor breakdown in the risk-tier view (Doc 02 §4: "Includes contributing-factor breakdown for auditability"); thresholds hard-coded, not pack-driven (RT4). Current rule is honest and fail-safe-closed (correct closure direction), just a small subset of the spec'd model.

Detailed description

This adapter connects the platform to payment rails for both collection and payout: Raast (PK), Aani (UAE), sarie/mada (KSA) and cross-border partners for the UAE→PK and KSA→PK corridors. It is the boundary the Payments saga relies on. Its two hard rules: every execution is idempotent, and a timeout is never assumed to be success or failure — it exposes an IN_FLIGHT state and a status-inquiry.

This ticket is EX1 — Payout execution (Must). The feature specification requires: Execute a payout on the bound rail; return accepted/in-flight/rejected.

Specified rules: Execution is idempotent by end-to-end id; the same instruction never pays twice. A timeout or ambiguous response returns IN_FLIGHT — never a guessed success/failure; the inquiry resolves it. KSA (sarie/mada) execution is pinned to the in-Kingdom path. Every rail binding conforms to the identical port shape (parity fixtures); every call carries tenant_id + app_id. Events: - Publishes/consumes: none directly (synchronous port + scheme callbacks normalized; statements feed 09). Design companion: **Impl (v3.1):** TypeScript — NestJS injectable providers, **one per rail**, in Payments (05) · **Docx:** `19_Adapter_Payout_Rail_Adapter_Specification.docx` Executes payout per corridor binding and exposes statements to Reconciliation (09). Launch rails: **Raast** (PK, SBP), **Aani** (AE, Al Etihad Payments/CBUAE), **sarie** (SA, SAMA) for domestic; a cross-border partner rail for UAE→PK / KSA→PK until direct scheme connectivity is.

What exists today: PayoutRailPort + SimulatedPayoutRailAdapter.executePayout. Remaining work to match the documentation: No real scheme send. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Regional sender rules matter at launch: PK/AE/SA SMS all require **registered sender IDs** and (PK notably) template pre-approval with the. Bindings (launch): `sms-primary` + `sms-secondary` (regional aggregators with PK/AE/SA reach), `email` (transactional ESP, per-tenant domain/DKIM), `push` (FCM/APNs via tenant app credentials), `mock` (sandbox).

This adapter provides authentication via OAuth2/OIDC with a realm per tenant, and the JwtTenantGuard that turns a validated token into an authenticated tenant/app/subject context. It ships as a client library (@platform/oidc) — not a deployable service — because it is a cross-cutting primitive imported by the gateway and every service. The tenant_id claim it establishes is what the entire isolation model keys on.

This ticket is AU1 — Token validation (JWKS) (Must). The feature specification requires: Validate signature/exp/audience against the realm JWKS.

Specified rules: Each tenant's users and clients are isolated in their own realm. JWKS are cached with correct rotation handling; a rotated key does not cause an outage. A request with a missing, expired or invalid tenant claim is rejected before any handler runs (fail closed). The guard exposes the same tenant/app/subject context contract everywhere it is imported. Events: - Publishes/consumes: none (library; realm bootstrap invoked by Control Plane, 12). Design companion: **Impl (v3.1):** TypeScript client library (`@platform/oidc`, openid-client-based) for all NestJS services + gateway; the two JVM islands (04, 10) validate with the equivalent Spring Security resource-server config against the **same realms** · **Docx:**. Authentication for platform operators, tenant staff, and end customers. **Realm-per-tenant** on the platform IdP (Keycloak reference); tenant-federated IdPs (their Azure AD/Okta) join via OIDC/SAML federation into that tenant's realm. Every access token carries `tenant_id` — the.

What exists today: packages/auth-kit HS256 verifyJwt. Rejects alg:none, tamper, wrong secret. 8 unit tests. ±60s skew. Remaining work to match the documentation: Not JWKS/openid-client. One shared AUTH_JWT_SECRET. No kid rotation. Stand-in (ADR-0006). Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes. Replace with real OIDC before any non-dev deployment.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Signature/exp/audience validation against per-realm JWKS; cached keys; rotation without outage.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: Asymmetric keys, JWKS endpoint/fetch/cache, kid rotation, aud/iss validation. The shared symmetric secret means any service holding it can mint arbitrary tokens for any tenant.

This net-new shared adapter computes the tax/levy lines the platform owes or collects: WHT and VAT on banking fees, and levies and VAT on takaful contributions and wakala fees. It is pure and deterministic — same inputs and same rule-pack version yield byte-identical output — with every line traceable to a named rule and pack version. It computes only; filing and remittance stay with Compliance Reporting (08) and.

This ticket is TX1 — computeLevies (Must). The feature specification requires: Return itemised tax/levy lines + total for an operation.

Specified rules: The sum of line amounts always equals the returned total (property-tested). Rules are data (versioned, effective-dated tables); rate changes are new rows, never edits to old ones. A country with no loaded pack fails closed at startup/health — never silently computes zero tax. All arithmetic uses @platform/money integer minor units; every call carries tenant_id + app_id. Events: control.config.published.v1. Design companion: **Impl:** TypeScript — pure rule-table computation on `@platform/money` (judged against the v3.1 JVM rule; eligible to move to a Java library like FX/17 if complexity grows — a packaging change, ports are language-agnostic) · **Owning squad:** Platform Adapters · **Status:** design draft · **Docx:**.

No meaningful implementation was found (No adapters/tax. Pricing currently emits TAX 0.00 (violates missing-pack ⇒ startup failure)). Implement this feature as specified. Concretely: computeLevies. SG1 — Create envelope

Not Started Medium Must Ready

E-Signature / Consent Adapter (26) · (no adapter)

Requirement / business context
Create a signing envelope over hashed documents + signers
Detailed description

This net-new shared adapter creates signing envelopes over documents, routes them to signers through the bound market scheme, tracks status, and — the part that matters legally — assembles and preserves the evidence bundle (who signed, authenticated how, when, document hashes, device/channel, certificate chain). It also captures standalone, revocable consents (e.g. bureau-inquiry consent) that other adapters verify.

This ticket is SG1 — Create envelope (Must). The feature specification requires: Create a signing envelope over hashed documents + signers.

Specified rules: Documents are hashed at envelope creation; any later byte change voids the envelope (loud tamper detection). The evidence bundle is written region-local before an envelope is reported complete (else it stays PENDING_EVIDENCE). Every call carries tenant_id + app_id; RTL documents (ur-PK Nastaliq, ar-*) render and hash deterministically. KSA evidence never leaves the Kingdom; retention follows the compliance pack. Events: esign.envelope.completed.v1. Design companion: **Impl:** TypeScript — NestJS injectable providers per signing scheme · **Owning squad:** Platform Adapters · **Status:** design draft · **Docx:** `26_Adapter_E_Signature_Consent_Adapter_Specification.docx` Signing envelopes + first-class consent records. Banking: account/loan/mandate agreements, bureau-inquiry consent. Takaful: policy documents, wakala agreement, claim forms. **The evidence bundle is the product** — who signed, authenticated how, when, document hashes.

No meaningful implementation was found (No adapter. Required before bureau (24). Outage queues, never downgrades signature level). Implement this feature as specified. Concretely: Create envelope. Evidence bundle written before completion, else PENDING_ENVELOPE.

Existing implementation

What was found in the repository: none found — repo-wide grep for SignaturePort/envelope/uaepass/nafath returns nothing outside docs; `adapters/AGENTS.md` lists `esign-consent` as a target only.

Transactional outbox events for Identity

Not Started High Must Ready

Identity (02)

Requirement / business context
Design 02 publishes identity.customer.registered.v1, verification.completed.v1, risk_tier.changed.v1.
Detailed description

This service is the system of record for customers (retail) and businesses (corporate/KYB), and for the verification cases that prove their identity. It computes and maintains a risk tier per customer from verification outcomes, screening signals, geography and product, and it drives the onboarding workflow from first application to activated relationship. Everything it does is scoped by the tenant's assigned.

This ticket is a documented platform requirement (Must): Design 02 publishes identity.customer.registered.v1, verification.completed.v1, risk_tier.changed.v1.

Specified rules: Every customer and business is uniquely and immutably identified; identity keys are the national IDs per market, never free-text names. Risk tier is recomputed deterministically whenever an input changes; the same inputs always yield the same tier. A verification-case timeout or provider error moves the case to MANUAL_REVIEW; the service never auto-approves on failure (fail-safe). Verification evidence (images, biometrics) is stored only as an object-storage reference; PII blobs never sit inline in the service database. Contract surface: - POST /v1/customers · POST /v1/customers/{id}/verifications · POST /v1/verifications/{caseId}/evidence. - GET /v1/customers/{id}/risk-tier · POST /v1/businesses/{id}/ubos. - GET /v1/customers/{id}/onboarding (status + SLA). Events: identity.customer.registered.v1, identity.verification.completed.v1, identity.risk_tier.changed.v1, screening.case.resolved.v1. Design companion: **Runtime:** NestJS 10 / TS strict · **Squad:** Identity & Onboarding · **DB:** PostgreSQL 16 · **Docx:** `02_Service_Identity_KYC_KYB_Onboarding_Service.docx`

No meaningful implementation was found (No Kafka producer in services/identity). Implement this feature as specified. Concretely: Outbox + publisher matching Ledger/Payments shape.

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Publish `identity.customer.registered.v1`, `identity.verification.completed.v1`, `identity.risk_tier.changed.v1` via transactional outbox with the mandatory envelope (event_id, tenant_id, correlation_id, causation_id, …).

This is the tenant-agnostic control plane and one of the eight shared adapters. It holds the tenant registry, the hierarchical configuration store and resolver, entitlements, and onboarding orchestration — and it holds no regulated customer data. Its hot path, resolveEffectiveConfig, is a dependency of every other service, so it is engineered for a <5 ms p99 and fails safe on cache-stale rather than hard-failing the.

This ticket is a documented platform requirement (Must): control.tenant.registered|activated|suspended.v1 and control.config.published.v1 (cache invalidation).

Specified rules: Destructive tenant transitions and config publishes require maker-checker. The control plane holds no regulated customer data and runs pooled, single-region-primary — the inverse posture to the data planes it manages. Config versions are immutable and effective-dated; publishing creates a new version rather than editing. Consumers fail safe on a stale cache read; the resolver never hard-fails the whole platform on a live-lookup miss. This ticket is a documented platform requirement (Must): ledger.hold.placed|captured|released.v1. Payments spec consumes captured/released (Payments README deliberately skipped — Ledger does not emit them).

Specified rules: A journal that does not balance to zero per currency is rejected in the domain and never persisted. This ticket is a documented platform requirement (Must): ADR-0005: CoA pack materializes system accounts at onboarding. Design 12 orchestrates.

Specified rules: A cross-currency conversion is one journal whose currency groups each sum to zero, bridged by FX position accounts, with the spread recognised in the customer's funding currency. A journal that does not balance to zero per currency is rejected in the domain and never persisted. All amounts are integer minor units; no floating-point arithmetic exists anywhere in the service. Posting is idempotent: the same idempotency key yields the identical journal and never double-posts. Contract surface: - POST /v1/journals · POST /v1/holds · POST /v1/holds/{id}/capture|release. - GET /v1/accounts/{id}/balance · POST /v1/journals/{id}/reversal. Events: ledger.journal.posted.v1, ledger.journal.reversed.v1. Design companion: System of record for value. Double-entry, append-only; balances are projections. Nothing else on the platform may hold a balance. Stays on the JVM for BigDecimal/long-minor-unit exactness, ArchUnit, and throughput on the posting hot path.

What exists today: holds.suspense, settlement.raast, fees.revenue, settlement.suspense self-provision on first use. HardcodedPkCoaTemplateRepository is the same PK pack for every tenant. settlement.aani/sarie/xborder-partner missing. Remaining work to match the documentation: Bind pack per tenant from Control Plane; materialize remaining refs; add other-rail settlement accounts. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What was found in the repository: `GetSystemAccountService` (`GET /v1/accounts/system/{ref}`) self-provisions pack-valid refs on first use (existing-or-create); `HoldCommandService.ensureHoldsSuspenseAccount` self-provisions `holds.suspense`; pack-invalid refs → 404 `UnknownAccountRefException` (no rogue minting); `perCurrency=true` refs refuse self-provisioning. No onboarding-time materialization: Control Plane exists but the orchestration call into Ledger isn't wired (README L1.5 note).

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Control Plane orchestrates, Ledger executes, at onboarding, maker-checker; a typo'd ref must fail, never mint a rogue account.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: Lazy creation is the *opposite* of ADR-0005 #3's "no lazy creation" rule — currently a deliberate stopgap; per-currency expansion semantics (`fees.revenue.<ccy>`) still unpinned; no maker-checker. The unknown-ref-fails half of ADR-0005 #3 is honoured; the materialize-at-onboarding half is not. Self-provisioning was extended ref-by-ref (holds.suspense → settlement.raast → fees.revenue) as consumers needed them.

Partially Done Critical Must Ready

Infra & CI

Requirement / business context
Cross-tenant access is release-blocking P1. Suite against raw connection for pooled stores.
Detailed description

This ticket is a documented platform requirement (Must): Cross-tenant access is release-blocking P1. Suite against raw connection for pooled stores.

Design companion: Branch protection on `main`: PR required · approvals (1 app repos, 2 platform repos) · CODEOWNERS review · required checks green + up-to-date · linear history · no force push · signed commits · release tags restricted to release-managers team.

What exists today: jvm/ledger isolation/TenantIsolationTest.java (app + TB AccountsMustHaveTheSameLedger). In-memory fakes were fixed. No shared suite for TS services/RLS. Remaining work to match the documentation: Extend to every persistence-touching service; RLS bypass tests; missing-context rejection. Treat the current path as incomplete until every acceptance criterion passes.

Existing implementation

Correctness verdict: partially correct — something real exists, but it does not fully match the specification. Do not treat the current path as complete until every acceptance criterion passes.

What was found in the repository: `jvm/ledger/src/test/.../isolation/TenantIsolationTest.java` — two tenants against the same application services: B cannot read/reverse/capture/release A's data (indistinguishable "not found"); same idempotency key under two tenants never collides; same natural key opens distinct accounts. Fixing the in-memory fakes' missing tenant scoping was itself a finding. Cross-tenant TB transfer physically rejected, live-verified (README L5).

What 'correct' means per the documentation: Tenant-A-vs-B negative tests, run against the raw connection for pooled stores, on every persistence-touching PR.

What is not correct yet, or still missing: Suite runs against in-memory fakes, not the real Postgres adapters or a raw connection; no RLS-bypass attempts (no RLS exists); not a PR gate (no CI). The hermetic suite is honest about its own limits (javadoc); the real-adapter run is the missing half.

Source of this assessment: documentation-vs-code gap analysis for «§19.3 tenant-isolation test suite gating persistence-touching changes».

Gap / missing work
Extend to every persistence-touching service; RLS bypass tests; missing-context rejection.

  • Raw connection tests included for pool model

9. Open questions / clarifications

  • Silent zero tax vs fail-closed. Design 10/25 and invariant #8: missing tax pack ⇒ startup failure. Live Pricing quotes TAX 0.00. Doc 29 asks whether to ship an interim PK pack in Phase 4 or full adapter 25 in Phase 6. Do not ship PK live with silent zero tax.
  • Screen HOLD vs FAIL (05 CP1 / 03 CM2). MoSCoW says screen-fail cancels the quote and fails the transfer. Design 05 parks at COMPLIANCE_HOLD. CLOSE currently publishes nothing so the transfer stays parked. Product must define the permanent-block path.
  • Compensation C3 reachability. Spec requires reverse+refund after settlement failure. Payments README argues the shape makes C3 unreachable. Needs an ADR or a fault-injection test.
  • Who owns cached ledger balances? Feature spec 04 BL2 puts Redis on Ledger; Wallets already caches composed balances (06 BS2).
  • HTTP 202 vs synchronous 200 on POST /v1/transfers while the rail is simulated.
  • Object storage vendor for KYC evidence, statement PDFs, e-sign bundles, profile photos.
  • Idempotency interceptor vs natural keys — several READMEs defer a shared HTTP replay store.
  • Identity ScreeningPort still trivial even though Screening (03) exists — likely an outdated README, but the code path is still mock.
  • Fresh-tenant send-money after provision-tenant.mjs: Payments/Screening do not route to the silo Ledger/Wallets pair.
  • Takaful rows in feature specs (e.g. 02 OB4, 12 RG5) vs ADR-0003 banking-only repo — treated as Out of Scope here.
  • 8-repo catalog (Doc 28) vs Nx monorepo (ADR-0003) — accepted deviation; not a defect.
  • Debezium vs polling outbox — documented simplification in Ledger; not yet an ADR for the whole platform.
  • Certification stream: NADRA, Raast, SBP/FMU packs — Doc 29 says open in week 1; no evidence in-repo that paperwork started.
  • Unclear tasks (1): BANK-066.

10. Suggested implementation order

Follow Doc 23/29 critical path. Do not gold-plate Phase 1. External certification runs in parallel.

  1. Close fail-closed holes now: tax pack or startup fail (10 QT5 / 25); Isolation router + §19.3 on every store (14); wire Identity to real Screening (02 RT1).
  2. Foundation remaining (M1): Control Plane cache p99 (12 CF6) + config events; entitlements; audit_log; @platform/oidc realm-per-tenant (22); CI gates (Design 27).
  3. Walking skeleton hardening (M2): real document journey (stop auto-verify in BFF); evidence storage; Identity outbox; CoA pack binding per tenant.
  4. Compliance gate (M3): entity screening, list versions, decision tables, case queue UI, CLOSE→fail path, PK list fixtures.
  5. Money movement (M4): Raast binding + status inquiry; corridor config from Control Plane; beneficiary validation; remaining rail settlement accounts; Pricing←Control Plane schedules; Pact for Screening.
  6. PK go-live bar (M5): NADRA+Raast certified; SBP/FMU pack; Notification 13+21 for OTP/receipts; Reconciliation 09 one clean cycle; reporting 08 STR path; on-call/DR; production edge.
  7. Adapter platform (M6): tax/e-sign/bureau; dual-consumer Pact; consent 26→24.
  8. Deferred until licensed: Cards 07+20, CBS host 18. UAE then KSA planes after PK.
  9. Customer channels in parallel once APIs exist: statements UI, beneficiaries/IBAN send, locale/RTL, compliance console.

11. Agile ticket readiness

281 tasks are specified enough to become stories (acceptance criteria + doc refs + repo paths). 18 need a product/architecture answer first (section 9). 12 are engineering-ready but blocked on vendor/certification (NADRA, Raast, commercial FX, bureau, UAE Pass, Yakeen, Aani, sarie).

Recommended epic mapping: one epic per Doc 02–13 service and 14–26 adapter; stories = BANK-xxx rows. MoSCoW Must + Critical/High on the critical path are Sprint candidates. Could-priority and licensed-optional cards stay in the backlog, not the current PI.

Tasks marked Done should still be converted to regression tickets or simply linked as completed scope so the board shows the full picture — do not re-implement them.

Analysis limitations

  • Word extracts used OOXML text/tables; complex nested drawings and some numbering may be incomplete. Design.md companions were treated as the engineering source of truth where they exist.
  • Status is from source and service READMEs, not a fresh live E2E run in this session. READMEs claim live verification; that was trusted where it named exact endpoints and outcomes.
  • No security review, pen test, or production traffic exists (AGENTS.md §9). “Done” never means production-certified.
  • Feature specs say “nothing built yet” (they were written at design freeze). Implementation status comes from the repo, not those status tables.
  • UI field-level requirements are thin in the blueprints (headless core). Screen tasks are inferred from service APIs + existing apps, not from a dedicated UX spec (none was in the documentation folder besides brand/design-system in-repo).
  • Presenter script and PPTX were not mined for hidden requirements.
  • Temporary docx extracts under docs/_tmp_docx_extract/ were generated for this analysis and may be deleted; this HTML is the deliverable.
